questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is the one _____ won the award.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**who**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pronoun "**who**" is used as the subject of a verb in a relative clause.
 
• The sentence requires a subject to complete the relative clause ("won the award"), which refers back to "the one."
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **3** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"She is the one **who**__ won the award."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "which"** is incorrect because "which" is used for things, not people.
 
• **Option 2: "whom"** is incorrect because "whom" is used as the object of a verb or preposition, not as the subject.
 
• **Option 3: "whose"** is incorrect because "whose" is used to indicate possession, not as the subject of a verb.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Esoteric
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Common.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Esoteric"** means something that is intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest. (गूढ़)
 
 
• **Example:** The professor's lecture on quantum mechanics was so esoteric that only a few students could follow it.
 
 
• **"Common"** refers to something that is known or understood by many people; it is not rare or specialized. (सामान्य)
 
 
• **Example:** The flu is a common illness that affects millions of people every year.
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Esoteric'** is **'Common'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Common.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Arcane **(गोपनीय): Understood by few; mysterious or secret.
 
 
• **Example:** The arcane rituals of the ancient tribe were known only to a few elders.
 
 
 
• **Cryptic **(संदिग्ध): Having a meaning that is mysterious or obscure.
 
 
• **Example:** His cryptic response left everyone in the room puzzled.
 
 
 
• **Abstruse **(कठिन): Difficult to understand; obscure.
 
 
• **Example:** The philosopher's abstruse theories were difficult for the average person to comprehend.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She __always do__ her work in time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. always does .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is "She," which is a third person singular subject.
 
• When using third person singular subjects (he, she, it) in the present simple tense, the verb should have an **-s** on the end.
 
• The verb "do" becomes "does" when used with third person singular subjects.

Correct sentence: *She always **does** her work in time.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Always will done:** This option is grammatically incorrect because "will done" is not a correct verb form.
 
• **Always done:** This option is ungrammatical because "done" is a past participle and cannot function as a main verb without an auxiliary verb.
 
• **Always doing:** This option uses the continuous form of the verb, which does not fit the context of a habitual action.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of an adverb.

options.text: We are hardly ever late for work.
Chandni is late often for work.
They are usually late for work.
Mahesh and Mukesh are always late for work.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Adverbs of frequency** (always, often, usually, rarely, never) are typically placed before the main verb in a sentence.
 
• In the incorrect sentence, "often" is placed after the verb "is late," which is not the typical placement for an adverb of frequency.
 
• To correct the sentence, the adverb should come before the verb: "Chandni is often late for work."

Correct sentence: *Chandni is **often** late for work.*

• **They are usually late for work:** Correct usage. "Usually" is an adverb placed correctly before the main verb.
 
• **Mahesh and Mukesh are always late for work:** Correct usage. "Always" is an adverb placed correctly before the main verb.

questions.question: Select the sentence with an error in the adverb used.

options.text: They performed the task surprisingly well despite the challenges.
She had scarcely begun her speech when the microphone failed.
He spoke softly enough to avoid waking the baby.
The solution was applied so effective that it resolved the issue immediately.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. The solution was applied so effective that it resolved the issue immediately .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the given sentence is the use of the adverb "**effective**." The correct adverb should be "**effectively**."
 
• "**Effective**" is an adjective, whereas "effectively" is the adverb form that modifies the verb "was applied" correctly.
 
• To correct the sentence, replace "effective" with "effectively": "The solution was applied so effectively that it resolved the issue immediately."

Correct sentence: *The solution was applied so **effectively** that it resolved the issue immediately.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **They performed the task surprisingly well despite the challenges:** Correct usage. "Surprisingly" modifies the adverb "well."
 
• **She had scarcely begun her speech when the microphone failed:** Correct usage. "Scarcely" modifies the verb "begun."
 
• **He spoke softly enough to avoid waking the baby:** Correct usage. "Softly" modifies the verb "spoke."
